title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: PHYL'S LOG
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Phyllis Nygaard. Everybody calls her Phyl.
She is fifty-six, she runs the bait shop in Hayward, Wisconsin, and in thirty years on that lake, she has never once fallen in.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE FLYER
segments.quote: If you obey all the rules, you miss all the fun.
segments.author: Katharine Hepburn
lines: One spring morning, her nephew Cody taped a flyer by the nightcrawlers. Log rolling. Ladies over fifty. July.
Phyl laughed. Ladies my age sell the worms. We don't fall in the lake.
Her friend Darlene from the diner quoted the actress Katharine Hepburn:
If you obey all the rules, you miss all the fun.
So Phyl signed the flyer. Then she bought a wetsuit in a color called Bold Plum.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: ELEVEN SPLASHES
segments.quote: You're never too old to become younger.
segments.author: Mae West
lines: At her first practice, she fell in eleven times in eleven minutes.
A teenager on the dock asked, Ma'am, are you lost?
Dripping, Phyl remembered a line from the movie star Mae West:
You're never too old to become younger.
She climbed back on that log and laughed. The teenager looked worried.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: EYES UP
segments.quote: Keep your eyes on the stars, but your feet on the ground.
segments.author: Theodore Roosevelt
lines: Phyl kept staring at her own feet, and down she went.
Arnie, a seventy-nine-year-old retired logger, quoted President Theodore Roosevelt:
Keep your eyes on the stars, but your feet on the ground.
So she looked at a tall pine on the far shore. She stayed up ten whole seconds.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: HALF WATER
segments.quote: Remember you are half water. If you can't go through an obstacle, go around it. Water does.
segments.author: Margaret Atwood
lines: But she fought that log like it owed her money. Stiff as a fence post.
Her niece, a librarian, texted her a line from the Canadian writer Margaret Atwood:
Remember you are half water. If you can't go through an obstacle, go around it. Water does.
So Phyl stopped fighting. Little quick steps, going with the spin, like dancing on a rolling pin.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE LUCKY SOCKS
segments.quote: The harder I practice, the luckier I get.
segments.author: Jerry Barber
lines: In June, Phyl bought lucky socks and a lucky hat, and she started skipping practice.
Arnie shook his head and quoted the golfer Jerry Barber:
The harder I practice, the luckier I get.
So every dawn before the shop opened, Phyl rolled in the pond out back. The fish got used to her.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FINAL
segments.quote: A stumble is not a fall.
segments.author: Haitian proverb
lines: In July, two thousand people watched the final. Phyl against a seventy-year-old champion from Minnesota.
One foot slipped off. Her arms spun like a windmill. Cody yelled an old Haitian proverb:
A stumble is not a fall.
Phyl found the log again. Ten seconds later, Minnesota went in with a big splash.
Now Phyl teaches a Saturday class for ladies over fifty. They all wear Bold Plum.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Break a rule. Feel younger. Look up. Go with the flow. Practice. Keep your feet.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Break a rule. Feel younger. Look up. Go with the flow. Practice. Keep your feet.
I tried log rolling once. The log won. It's still bragging.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
